Today: 2026-02-10
Operations and engineering leads meeting - Tuesday 10 February 2026. Project of record: Basalt offline mode for the Ironbridge site-inspection app (contract deliverable for Hallam Construction). Other projects were covered in the second half.

Attendance: Martina Kovac (engineering manager), Femi Adebayo (mobile lead), Josh Whitaker (customer success, Hallam account), Nadia Rahman (QA), Ben Torres (operations). Notes: Nadia.

Basalt - background
Hallam's inspectors work in basements and new-build shells with no signal. The contract amendment signed in October commits us to offline inspections - create, edit, photograph and sign off - with automatic sync when the device reconnects, delivered to all Hallam users by March 1. The amendment carries a service-credit penalty if we miss it, so Josh asked for a clear read today.

Basalt - field pilot results
Femi summarised the three-week field pilot that ended on February 6 at two Hallam sites in Leeds and Sheffield. Thirty-one inspectors completed 486 inspections offline. Sync conflicts occurred on 0.6 percent of records, under the 1 percent threshold in the acceptance criteria, and every conflict was resolved by the merge screen without data loss. Photos queued offline uploaded successfully once devices reconnected, though very large batches took up to twelve minutes on site Wi-Fi. Nadia's regression suite passed on the pilot build with no open severity-1 or severity-2 defects.

Basalt - release plan
The store builds go out for review on February 17, and the release to all Hallam users is set for February 24, five days inside the March 1 commitment. Josh will tell Hallam's head of quality this afternoon. Ben confirmed the support rota is staffed for launch week, and the help-centre articles are drafted. Femi wants to improve photo-upload speed in a later release by compressing images on the device, which is outside the contract scope.

Other projects
- Ironbridge web dashboard redesign: about three weeks behind because the charting library upgrade broke the export to PDF; Martina expects a new date by Friday.
- Integration with the Quarrystone document-management system: waiting on Quarrystone to issue API keys; the partner has not responded to two emails.
- The proposed tablet kiosk for site offices was cancelled by the product council last week; there was not enough customer demand.
- Cost tracking module: on schedule for April.

Operations
Ben reported that the on-call load dropped by a third after last month's alert clean-up. The database upgrade for the EU region is booked for the night of February 21. Hosting costs rose 6 percent because of photo storage growth; Ben will look at lifecycle rules to move old photos to cheaper storage.

People
Nadia is on leave February 26 to March 6; Josh asked that launch issues go to the QA channel rather than directly to her. A new mobile engineer, Kai Lindgren, starts on March 2.

Decisions
1. Basalt store submission on February 17.
2. The photo-compression idea goes into the product backlog, not into this release.
3. Ben's storage lifecycle change goes ahead after the EU database upgrade.

Actions
- Josh: email Hallam's head of quality today.
- Femi: prepare release notes and the in-app "what's new" text.
- Martina: get a new date for the dashboard redesign.
- Ben: draft storage lifecycle rules.

Next meeting: Tuesday 24 February.

Today: 2026-04-27
Wren Labs - weekly hardware report, Friday 24 April 2026. This report is for the Wren AQ2 air-quality monitor (second-generation hardware), which is our project; the firmware platform and retail teams add short notes at the end.

Where AQ2 stands
The AQ2 schedule plans EVT (engineering validation) units in May, DVT in July and mass production in September for the US school-district contract. Industrial design is frozen. The enclosure tooling at our moulding partner in Dongguan passed its first-article inspection on April 16 with only a minor gate-mark issue, which has been polished out.

Electronics
Rev B of the main board came back from the fab on April 13. Power consumption in sleep is 38 microamps, under the 50 microamp target, which gives the battery version the 18 months the district asked for. The PM2.5 laser sensor and the temperature/humidity sensor are reading correctly against the reference instruments in our chamber.

Supply
This is the problem area. The NDIR carbon-dioxide sensor we designed around comes from a single supplier in Sweden. On April 20 the supplier told us it has suspended all shipments to contract manufacturers in China while it waits for an export-licence ruling on a component in the sensor's optical module, and it cannot say when the ruling will come. Without that sensor we cannot build a single EVT unit; CO2 is the core measurement the school districts are buying, so building boards without it would not validate anything. Mihail checked the two alternative sensors on the market: both have a different footprint and a different supply voltage, and neither has the accuracy certificate the contract specifies, so switching would mean a board redesign plus new certification, which we are not doing at this stage. Our EVT kits sit at the contract manufacturer with every part except the CO2 sensor. We have asked whether the sensors could ship to our office in Oregon instead and be hand-carried, and the supplier says the suspension covers that route too.

Firmware
The firmware team has the AQ2 build running on Rev B boards fed by the lab sensor rig. Over-the-air update of the sensor calibration tables works. The cloud dashboard shows the new CO2 trend view, though it is fed by simulated data for now.

Certification
FCC and IC pre-scans are scheduled with the test lab, but the lab needs complete EVT units, so the booking is provisional.

Other teams
- Firmware platform: the shared Bluetooth stack update is two weeks late; it is not needed for AQ2, which uses Wi-Fi only.
- Retail: the plan to sell the first-generation AQ1 through a big-box chain was cancelled on April 22 after the chain changed its margin terms. The AQ1 stays on our web store.
- Cloud: the data-export API for district facility managers shipped on Tuesday.

Finance
Spend is 4 percent under the AQ2 budget for the year to date. Holding the EVT kits at the contract manufacturer costs a small storage fee per week.

Next week
Ana will keep pressing the Swedish supplier's sales director for a ruling date and will report the moment anything changes. Mihail will document the alternative-sensor comparison in case the board revisits it. The enclosure team will finish the light-pipe sample.
